candidate.blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity — assess psychosocial status, identify mental-health concerns, provide emotional support, and facilitate appropriate referrals/resources
candidate.blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — postpartum mental health / parental role adaptation
candidate.educational_objective: Support postpartum psychosocial adaptation by screening for depression and anxiety with a validated tool and ensuring timely follow-up when symptoms or screening results are concerning.

options.A: Use a standardized, validated depression/anxiety screening instrument and ensure abnormal results receive timely assessment and follow-up
options.B: Reassure the client that all mood changes after birth are normal and do not require screening
options.C: Focus only on the newborn because parental emotional health is outside postpartum care
options.D: Advise the client to wait until symptoms have lasted several months before discussing them with a clinician

candidate.rationale: ACOG recommends screening people receiving postpartum care for depression and anxiety with standardized, validated instruments and implementing screening within a system that provides timely assessment, diagnosis, treatment, monitoring, and follow-up based on severity. Persistent loss of pleasure and feeling overwhelmed warrant assessment rather than normalization or delay. Parental mental health is an integral part of postpartum care. Therefore A is the best answer.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Postpartum mental-health symptoms should be assessed with validated depression/anxiety screening and positive/concerning findings should lead to timely follow-up rather than reassurance or delay.
candidate.source_document_title: Patient Screening — Perinatal Mental Health; Optimizing Postpartum Care
candidate.source_locator: Patient Screening: screen everyone receiving postpartum care for depression and anxiety using standardized validated instruments; screening must be paired with systems for timely assessment, diagnosis, treatment, monitoring and follow-up. Optimizing Postpartum Care > Mood and emotional well-being: screen for postpartum depression/anxiety with a validated instrument and provide support/resources
candidate.source_organization: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG)
candidate.source_version_date: ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline No. 4 framework (June 2023) and current implementation guidance; pages accessed 2026-08-17
candidate.stem: At a postpartum follow-up visit, a client reports feeling persistently overwhelmed and no longer enjoying activities that were previously pleasurable. Which nursing action best supports safe psychosocial adaptation to parenthood?
